AppleSentimentAnalyzer: Runs Apple's English paragraph sentiment baseline on its worker. It accepts no history, returns valence only and supplies no calibrated confidence. Unsupported language/context/structure and missing or invalid tagger output throw QualiaError; none becomes a neutral fallback. Construction does not require a downloaded model.
FallbackAnalyzer: Attempts the primary analyzer first and consults only the explicitly configured fallback causes. Installation rejects incompatible contracts. Cancellation and nonselected failures propagate. A successful result retains the actual leaf analyzer identity; it is not relabelled as the primary.
QualiaInput: Represents current text plus optional oldest-to-newest historical fragments and optional declared language. Construction rejects blank text with emptyInput. Direct analyzers may accept context; a session requires external context to be empty because it owns history. Input IDs must be unique within an accepted session sequence. Text and IDs are sensitive.
QualiaInputID: Stores the caller's exact, nonblank identifier. Equality is case-sensitive and performs no trimming or Unicode normalization. Construction and decoding reject blank identifiers with invalidInputID. Do not log IDs as diagnostic metadata.
QualiaScore: Both value and optional confidence must be finite in the closed range 0...1; violations throw invalidScore or invalidConfidence. Missing confidence is not zero confidence, and confidence scales need independent calibration across analyzers. Decoding applies the same validation as construction.
QualiaObservation: Carries the original input ID, resolved language, actual producing analyzer and declared semantic outputs. An absent signal is not a measured zero. The session checks output against the analyzer's stable capabilities. This value can contain sensitive semantic information and is not a redacted diagnostic payload.
QualiaSession: Retain this actor for one accepted event stream. configured installs explicit components; sentimentPreview requires valence and haptic playback; horrorNarrative validates narrative signals and continuous playback. New processing supersedes older work. process throws input/preparation/analyzer/lifecycle failures; a returned response can separately contain execution.failure. Await suspend/resume/reset and preference updates, and stop admitting input while cleanup is pending or failed. Resume never replays old input.
QualiaResponse: Separates an analyzer observation, temporal transition, policy plan and attempted execution. A planned command does not prove successful rendering. Inspect execution.failure and command outcomes even when process returned successfully. Physical sensation requires a real device; a response is not safe to serialize into diagnostics.
QualiaLanguageResolver: Resolves language using requireExplicit, detect or preferExplicitThenDetect. Detection requires an allowed-language set and a minimum confidence in 0...1. Missing, low-confidence and unsupported language are distinct failures. Resolution is preparation, not a promise that a selected model supports the language.
QualiaContextWindow: Retains a contiguous newest suffix of whole historical fragments within fragment, Character and optional UTF-8 limits. Current text and IDs are never sliced or normalized. Current text alone exceeding a bound throws currentTextExceedsContextBounds; arithmetic overflow throws contextSizeOverflow. Trim diagnostics report before/after counts, not text.
QualiaContextConfiguration: maximumFragments counts historical fragments only and may be zero. maximumCharacters counts extended grapheme clusters including current text and must be positive. Optional maximumUTF8Bytes also includes current text and must be positive when present. Invalid bounds throw invalidContextConfiguration; these bounds do not approximate model tokens.
QualiaSceneReducer: Consumes the previous state, current observation and an injected monotonic instant to compute a new transition without rendering. Continuous evidence affects state over time, whereas impact/shock belong to the current transition. Missing values do not become zeros. The resulting phase is derived state, not a new model label.
HorrorNarrativePolicy: Strict installation requires suspense, threat and an accent signal (impact or shock), plus continuous haptics. The policy plans owned ambient heartbeat start/replacement/stop separately from one-shot accents. Configuration controls confidence, thresholds and mapping; it never infers signals from text or sentiment. Runtime preferences and the executor can further suppress planned playback.
SentimentPulsePolicy: Maps valence sufficiently far from neutral to a short accent. It requires valence and haptic playback at installation. Missing/insufficient evidence, cooldowns and preferences can produce no command. Positive/negative valence is not suspense, threat or a measurement of the reader's emotion.
NoReactionPolicy: Produces an empty haptic plan while allowing analysis and state transitions. Use it with NoOpHapticRenderer for an explicitly analysis-only integration. It does not silently replace a failed or incompatible physical policy.
HeartbeatPatternFactory: Creates validated heartbeat descriptors from supplied parameters and a maximum duration. It performs no playback or text analysis. Use the public factory in policies rather than copying rhythm math; test expected command descriptors against independent literals.
CoreHapticRenderer: MainActor-owned adapter for physical Core Haptics playback. Check capabilities before installing a policy. Effect ownership and channels separate ambient loops from accents. Engine interruption/reset and command failures remain observable; inspect activeEffects after a partial failure and complete cleanup before reusing the session. Unsupported hardware is not evidence of tactile quality.
NoOpHapticRenderer: Implements the renderer boundary without generating a physical effect. Its capabilities must not be used to claim hardware support or satisfy a strict physical policy. Pair it with an explicit no-reaction configuration for analysis-only flows; use RecordingHapticRenderer when tests need command capture.
QualiaHapticPreferences: Controls enabled state, continuous effects, intensity scale and maximum continuous duration independently of semantic policy. Update through the session so disabling feedback also stops owned effects. The host maps Reduce Motion and its own controls into these values; the runtime does not read UI preferences automatically.
QualiaReactionExecutor: Runs on MainActor and applies safety, ownership and deadline constraints to an ordered plan. A later command may fail after an earlier command succeeded; attempted outcomes and active renderer state determine the reconciled applied state. Never commit a policy's intended state as if every physical command succeeded.
QualiaDecisionReport: Formats the tail of an already-redacted diagnostic snapshot into human-readable lines. maximumEvents must be in 1...4096 or construction throws invalidConfiguration. omittedEventCount counts this formatter's exclusions, not earlier sink drops. Formatting is synchronous, actor-neutral and transport-free; text wording is not a stable serialization schema.
FixtureAnalyzer: Looks up explicitly authored observations by input ID and preserves their provenance. Unknown IDs throw missingFixture; fixtures never classify unseen text. Construction validates the fixture contract. Use fixed observations to test session behavior, not to claim semantic model accuracy.
ControlledAnalyzer: An actor with numbered pending requests and explicit completion barriers for deterministic concurrency tests. waitForRequest observes admission; complete resolves a selected request. Cancellation behavior is configurable for stale-result tests. Cancel remaining requests at teardown; clearHistory does not synthesize completion.
RecordingHapticRenderer: MainActor test renderer that records command history, owner/channel activity and injected failures. It can simulate interruptions and resets without Core Haptics. Exact command equality validates orchestration; it cannot establish actuator timing, comfort or physical sensation.
QualiaSessionHarness: MainActor consumer helper that owns a real public session, recording renderer, deterministic clock and diagnostics. Process inputs with optional explicit time advancement, assert exact ordered descriptors and reset at teardown. The harness supplies no semantic oracle; expected commands must be independently authored.
TestQualiaClock: Synchronized manually advanced monotonic time. advance rejects negative movement; sleep and waitUntilSleeping provide cancellation-aware test barriers. Advance time or cancel waiters explicitly rather than relying on wall-clock sleeps. cancelAll releases pending test work for teardown.
RecordingQualiaDiagnosticsSink: Synchronized bounded test storage for structured events. A full sink drops newest events and increments droppedEventCount; its snapshot does not recover those events. Use a separate bounded report window for presentation and keep both loss counts visible.
CoreMLQualiaAnalyzer: Asynchronously resolves and validates local model assets, compiles/loads Core ML and isolates inference on its worker. Capabilities come from the validated adapter manifest. Manifest, checksum, tensor, tokenization and transformation failures are explicit; no arbitrary LABEL number is assigned narrative meaning. Cancellation is preserved around work that cannot be interrupted internally.
BundledQualiaModelSource: Locates an asset directory relative to the supplied bundle's resources. subdirectory and manifestName must describe safe local paths. Missing or incompatible assets fail setup; resolution does not download files or grant redistribution rights. The analyzer subsequently validates the resolved manifest and inventory.
FileQualiaModelSource: Resolves an explicitly supplied local directory and manifest name. Remote URLs and unsafe asset layouts are rejected by the model-source/validation boundary. The caller owns asset provenance, licensing and access; no conversion or network fetch occurs during resolution.
